question: Tell me about something you learned during your studies.
answer:
One thing I learned during my studies was how much my approach changes when I stop trying to do everything alone and actually talk things through with other people. In one of my coursework projects, we had to work on a group assignment, and at first I thought it would just be easier to handle my part quietly and keep moving. But after a while I realized that if we didn’t check in with each other, we ended up repeating work or missing small things.

It also taught me that I’m not always going to get things right the first time, and that’s okay. I got better at asking questions earlier instead of waiting until I was stuck. I think that was a useful lesson for me, because it made me more comfortable with being unsure and just learning as I go.

What stood out to me was that communication matters a lot more than I expected. Even simple things like checking in, asking questions early, and making sure everyone understood the plan made a difference. I also learned that it’s okay not to know everything straight away, because part of studying is figuring things out as you go and being willing to adjust. That experience made me more comfortable working with other people and more aware of how I approach tasks.

I also learned that different people approach the same assignment in very different ways, and that can make the whole process better.

Overall, it made me more comfortable with group work and more aware that learning is not just about getting the right answer, but also about building understanding step by step.

So overall, I think I learned that studying is not just about getting through the material, but about building a better way of thinking and working through things step by step.

question: Tell me about a project where planning was the main activity.
answer:

I was part of the group discussions, but I stayed mostly in the background and helped by listening, organizing ideas, and making sure everyone’s suggestions were included. The main challenge was getting everyone aligned, because we all had slightly different ideas at the start. We spent time talking through the options, comparing what was realistic, and narrowing it down to one plan we all felt good about.

What I learned from it was that planning is really about communication and cooperation. Even without actually carrying out the event, the planning stage mattered a lot because it helped the group feel clear and coordinated. In the end, we came away with a shared direction and a better sense of how to work together.

Overall, it made me more confident in group settings and more aware of how important it is to stay organized and respectful when working with others.

That experience made me more confident in group settings, and it showed me the value of patience, listening, and clear communication.
